visual.general_description: Flowchart of boxes and arrows with two printed call scripts below it, describing an ECLS heads-up process.
visual.detailed_description: A black-and-white flowchart on a white background. The top box is titled "Indications" and lists "Myocarditis, acute respiratory failure with oxygenation index > 20, congenital diaphragmatic hernia, shock with lactic acidosis, multiple organ failure, high-dose inotropes/vasoactive agents". Two arrows leave it diagonally downward to the left box "Physician Role" ("Notify ECLS Physician, cardiologist, and surgeon. Discuss the case, cannulation strategy, consider femoral vein and arterial line placements, and indications to initiate ECLS.") and the right box "Nursing Role" ("Notify blood bank, ECLS perfusionist, OR team, and pharmacist. Ensure CBC, type and screen, bed position appropriate for the surgeon to cannulate, NG, and foley"). Two arrows from those boxes converge on the central box "Ongoing care" ("Daily evaluation for heads-up status. Central venous and arterial line maintenance, utilizing them for patient care. Other management strategies for patient care"). One arrow leads down to the bottom box reading "Patient goes on ECLS or Comes off Heads-up status". Below the boxes, text headed "Script for First Call:" and "Script for Second Call:" gives two quoted spoken scripts, one a heads-up call and one an ECLS activation call. No patient name, identifier, date or image of a patient is visible.
